_meta.status: RESEARCHED ADDITIONAL RECORDS - structured from authoritative medical sources
_meta.note: These records are structured knowledge-base abstractions for patient routing. They are not diagnoses or prescriptions. Baseline tests are clinician-directed considerations, not mandatory tests.
_meta.source_policy: Sources limited to NHS, WHO and Mayo Clinic pages identified in the source field. Verify source pages and clinically review the records before production deployment.
_meta.nhs_attribution: Information from the NHS website is licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.

red_flags: persistent vomiting or severe abdominal swelling
records.age_notes: Children and older adults may need age-specific assessment; infants require pediatric advice.
baseline_tests: Usually clinical assessment only
Blood tests or other investigations if persistent or another cause is suspected

red_flags: very high temperature with meningitis symptoms
records.age_notes: Children and adolescents with recurrent migraine should be assessed by a clinician experienced in pediatric headache.
records.gender_notes: Pregnancy or recent childbirth with a severe migraine-like headache needs urgent assessment.
baseline_tests: Clinical history and neurological examination
Brain imaging only when clinically indicated

records.age_notes: Young children with feeding difficulty or breathing through the mouth should be assessed by a clinician.
baseline_tests: Clinical assessment of symptoms and nasal/face examination
Further imaging or specialist assessment if persistent, recurrent or complicated

red_flags: swelling of lips tongue or throat
records.age_notes: Children can develop hay fever; persistent symptoms should be assessed by a clinician.
baseline_tests: Usually clinical assessment
Allergy testing if the diagnosis or trigger is unclear and testing is clinically indicated

red_flags: swelling of lips tongue face or throat
records.age_notes: Children with suspected food or medicine allergy should be assessed by a pediatric clinician; severe reactions require emergency care.
baseline_tests: Clinical assessment
Allergy testing when indicated

records.age_notes: Atopic eczema commonly begins in childhood; children should be assessed if symptoms are persistent or severe.
baseline_tests: Clinical skin examination
Additional testing only if another diagnosis or infection is suspected

records.age_notes: Acne is common in adolescents but can occur at any age; severe or scarring acne warrants medical assessment.
baseline_tests: Usually clinical skin examination
Further tests only when another underlying cause is suspected

records.age_notes: Risk increases with age; blood pressure screening is important in adults.
baseline_tests: Blood pressure measurement
Repeat or ambulatory/home blood pressure measurement when clinically indicated
Blood and urine tests may be used to assess associated risk or causes

records.age_notes: Older adults and people taking blood-pressure medicines may need assessment for postural hypotension.
records.gender_notes: Pregnancy can be associated with lower blood pressure and should be assessed in context.
baseline_tests: Blood pressure measurement
Blood pressure measurement after changing position when postural hypotension is suspected
Blood tests or ECG if an underlying cause is suspected

records.care_category: Possible kidney stone / urinary tract stone
records.age_notes: Children and adolescents with suspected stones need pediatric assessment and age-appropriate imaging.
records.gender_notes: Pregnancy changes the preferred imaging approach; urgent clinical assessment is appropriate.
baseline_tests: Urine test
Blood tests for kidney function and relevant substances
Ultrasound or CT when clinically indicated

records.age_notes: Persistent or recurrent symptoms in older adults warrant medical assessment.
records.gender_notes: Pregnancy can cause indigestion; medication and investigation choices should be clinician-guided.
baseline_tests: Usually clinical assessment
H. pylori testing if clinically indicated
Endoscopy if persistent symptoms or alarm features warrant it

red_flags: very high temperature with feeling unwell
records.age_notes: Persistent rectal bleeding should not automatically be attributed to piles, particularly in older adults.
baseline_tests: Clinical examination
Further examination or tests if the diagnosis is uncertain or bleeding needs another cause excluded

records.age_notes: Children with significant injuries should be assessed because growth plates can be affected.
baseline_tests: Physical examination
X-ray if fracture is suspected

red_flags: burn on face genitals or buttocks
records.age_notes: Children with burns should receive prompt clinical assessment; young children can deteriorate with significant burns.
baseline_tests: Clinical assessment of burn depth and extent
Blood tests or imaging only when clinically indicated for significant burns

records.age_notes: Children with recurrent or persistent mouth ulcers may need pediatric or dental assessment.
baseline_tests: Oral examination
Blood tests if ulcers are recurrent, persistent or an underlying deficiency/systemic condition is suspected

red_flags: not starting to heal within 10 days
records.age_notes: A newborn exposed to an active cold sore requires urgent medical advice.
records.gender_notes: Pregnancy warrants clinician advice if lesions are severe or recurrent.
baseline_tests: Usually clinical examination
Swab or other testing only if the diagnosis is uncertain

records.age_notes: Newborns with red or sticky eyes require prompt medical assessment.
baseline_tests: Eye examination
Eye swab only when clinically indicated, such as selected persistent or unusual infections

records.age_notes: Older adults with new vertigo and falls need prompt assessment.
baseline_tests: Clinical balance and neurological assessment
Positional testing when appropriate
Hearing assessment or imaging if clinically indicated

red_flags: symptoms suggesting severe sleep apnoea or breathing pauses
records.age_notes: Children and adolescents with persistent sleep problems should be assessed using age-appropriate sleep guidance.
baseline_tests: Sleep and medical history
Sleep diary when useful
Sleep study only when another sleep disorder such as sleep apnoea is suspected

records.age_notes: Children and pregnant people require age- and pregnancy-specific haemoglobin assessment.
records.gender_notes: Heavy menstrual bleeding can contribute to iron deficiency and should be assessed when relevant.
baseline_tests: Full blood count / haemoglobin
Iron studies when iron deficiency is suspected
Further tests guided by the suspected cause

red_flags: inability to speak normally because of breathlessness
records.age_notes: Asthma commonly begins in childhood; children need pediatric assessment when symptoms are recurrent.
records.gender_notes: Pregnancy requires review of asthma control and treatment by a clinician.
baseline_tests: Clinical assessment and chest examination
Spirometry or another breathing test when appropriate
Peak-flow monitoring may be used

red_flags: blue or grey lips or skin
records.age_notes: Young children, adults over 65 and people with significant heart or lung disease have higher risk of severe pneumonia.
baseline_tests: Clinical examination and oxygen assessment
Chest X-ray when clinically indicated
Blood tests when needed to assess severity or alternative diagnoses

red_flags: new weakness or loss of movement
records.age_notes: Children under 5 and people with weakened immune systems have increased risk of serious TB disease.
baseline_tests: Rapid molecular diagnostic test when TB disease is suspected
Sputum testing
Chest X-ray or other imaging as clinically indicated

records.age_notes: Infants, children under 5 and pregnant people are at higher risk of severe malaria.
records.gender_notes: Pregnancy increases the risk of severe malaria and needs prompt medical assessment.
baseline_tests: Malaria diagnostic test / blood test
Further blood tests to assess severity when clinically indicated

records.age_notes: Children require prompt assessment if warning signs develop.
records.gender_notes: Pregnancy warrants prompt medical assessment for suspected dengue.
baseline_tests: Dengue laboratory testing as clinically indicated and according to illness timing
CBC / platelet count may be used to monitor illness severity

records.age_notes: Very young children and older adults are at higher risk of severe influenza.
records.gender_notes: Pregnant people are a higher-risk group and should seek medical advice promptly when significantly unwell.
baseline_tests: Usually clinical assessment
Influenza testing when clinically indicated, especially when the result would change management

records.age_notes: Older adults and people with underlying conditions may have higher risk of severe disease.
records.gender_notes: Pregnancy can alter risk and treatment considerations; seek clinician advice when unwell.
baseline_tests: COVID-19 diagnostic testing when clinically indicated
Oxygen saturation assessment when respiratory symptoms are present

red_flags: pain spreading to the back with vomiting
records.age_notes: Children with suspected gallstones need pediatric assessment.
records.gender_notes: Gallstones are more common in women; pregnancy may affect investigation choices.
baseline_tests: Abdominal ultrasound
Blood tests when complications or liver/biliary disease are suspected

records.care_category: Acute inflammatory joint pain / possible gout
red_flags: high fever with hot swollen joint
records.age_notes: Children with suspected gout need specialist assessment because gout is uncommon in children.
baseline_tests: Clinical joint assessment
Serum urate may be measured
Joint fluid examination may be required when diagnosis is uncertain or infection must be excluded

records.care_category: Jaundice / possible liver or biliary disorder
red_flags: new yellowing of skin or eyes
records.age_notes: Newborn jaundice has a separate assessment pathway and should be evaluated by a pediatric/newborn clinician.
records.gender_notes: Pregnancy-associated jaundice requires prompt medical assessment.
baseline_tests: Liver function blood tests
Bilirubin measurement
Additional blood tests and abdominal imaging guided by the suspected cause

records.age_notes: Older adults and people with heart, kidney or liver conditions need assessment of the underlying cause.
records.gender_notes: Pregnancy can cause oedema, but sudden or severe swelling needs prompt assessment.
baseline_tests: Clinical examination and blood pressure
Blood tests for kidney/liver/heart-related causes when indicated
ECG or imaging when clinically indicated
records.source: NHS: Swollen ankles, feet and legs (oedema) - https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/oedema/

records.age_notes: Children and adolescents with suspected thyroid disease require age-specific assessment.
records.gender_notes: Pregnancy or plans for pregnancy require prompt thyroid assessment and monitoring.
baseline_tests: Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)
Free thyroxine (T4) when indicated
Further thyroid tests based on clinician assessment

red_flags: very fast or irregular heartbeat with severe symptoms
records.age_notes: Children and adolescents need age-specific thyroid assessment.
records.gender_notes: Pregnancy changes the evaluation and treatment approach; clinician assessment is important.
baseline_tests: Thyroid function blood test including TSH and T4/T3 as indicated
Further antibody tests or thyroid imaging when clinically indicated
